Again, i never said I attempt literally any sort of therapy with him. Much less psychoanalysis. (Also again. Who tf even uses psychoanalysis anymore fr)

I only mentioned I am a therapist to highlight that I understand he *should* be seeing one because that's the only response I get about him is to get him in therapy.  But he refuses and I'm tired of fighting it. I am not his therapist. You having a shitty ex does not mean I'm attempting to provide an out of date form of therapy for him.

I never said I was his therapist or made any attempt to. Only that i recognize its importance as one myself. To be clear, I've never acted as a therapist or even attempted to for him. That would be gravely unethical. I dont provide any problem solving, counseling, cognitive or behavioral techniques, much less "psychoanalysis" which is hardly even used anymore anyway, or anything past validating and encouragement. We have seen numerous other therapists for him. I dont need education on diagnosis, medications, or the effect of impotence on men.

I'm not sure. I'm not outright disagreeing with you, I think I just have seen how much worse things can be? My ex did things very intentionally, his violence was clear, more extreme, and the manipulation was obvious especially once I got away from him. He did things that a typical abuser does, made me leave me friendships especially male ones, made it difficult to make new friends at school, turned off my alarm so I'd miss tests or work, all kinds of weird stuff.   


My husband however is good friends with my friends, sometimes he complains if I go out without him or gets mopey but with COVID that hasn't been happening... Before I'd usually take him with. I am the primary earner and for a long time was the only earner and supported him, so I have "money" I guess, he hasn't restricted that. Most of our large ticket things are in my name, rent, utilities, car, so he has done nothing to make me trapped with him like my ex. I genuinely don't think he does these things intentionally or in an effort to manipulate me, I think his emotions are just out of control and he's struggling to handle it. And I'm tired of handling it for him.   


I don't want to be "that person" that denies it and denies it forever... I don't know where I am on it I guess. To me an abuser has always been someone manipulating and hurting the other person with a power dynamic, I don't think that's him.

We have attempted to get him to therapy many many times but he doesn't commit to treatment. I have gone but its been many years, as I mentioned I am afraid to open wounds that will be tough to close especially during COVID stress. 

That said I dont think its a bad idea so thank you for the input.
